cohort: The study included 100 pregnant women who were under 20 years of age and delivered at a tertiary care center over a three-year period (2018-2021).
finding: Teenage pregnancies are associated with specific concerns such as pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH), preterm births, and a chance of cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD).
mod_finding: 31% of mothers had a lower segment cesarean section (LSCS), highlighting an increased rate of LSCS in teenage pregnancies.
